human_economic_burden.boundary: Present exposure, not realized annual victims or future exposure.

extent.geographic_scope: global low-lying coasts and coastal communities
extent.boundary: Global coastal scope; no inference of uniform hazard or protection.

source_locators: WMO State of the Climate 2025 Update: nearly 11 percent of the global population, around 900 million people, live on low-lying coasts directly exposed to coastal hazards.
WMO State of the Climate 2025 Update: sea-level rise rate increased from 2.1 mm/year in 1993-2002 to 4.1 mm/year in 2016-2025.
UNEP: coastal-flood extent increased over 20 years, leaving 14 million more people with a 1-in-20 annual flooding chance.

transformations.formula: Calculate the percentage increase from the WMO 1993-2002 global mean sea-level rate to the 2016-2025 rate.
Normalize WMO current low-lying-coast exposure; retain the UNEP additional 1-in-20 exposure as context and never add overlapping populations.
Normalize the 32-year satellite assessment period and retain global coastal scope without uniform-hazard inference.

receipts.uncertainty: Low-lying-coast and coastal-flood exposure depend on elevation, population, protection and hazard models. Preliminary 2025 sea-level data are affected by natural variability. Exposure is not realized annual displacement or loss.
receipts.freshness: WMO 2025 update and UNEP 2026 coastal-exposure statement; snapshot captured 2026-07-31T18:27:29.012Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: WMO and UNEP quantify observed global hazard acceleration, present exposed population, multi-decadal persistence and worldwide coastal extent.
higher_priority_failures: The operational NOAA CO-OPS snapshot is a selected-station panel and cannot defensibly aggregate current global coastal inundation exposure.
